item.title: Evidence of a federal crime? We will know soon!
item.description: Senator John Boozman claims he spoke with Mitch McConnell on the night of August 5 and received authorization to cast McConnell’s proxy votes the following day. That makes one question extremely important: Was Mitch McConnell actually capable of speaking with Boozman and authorizing those votes on August 5? If McConnell was unable to communicate and did not authorize those votes, then Boozman’s statement would be false and votes were attempted in a U.S. Senate committee in another senator’s name without his authorization. Could that constitute a federal crime? If so, it needs to be investigated. There should be a written record. Release McConnell’s proxy authorization and put this question to rest. The American people deserve proof that the votes being cast in the United States Senate are actually authorized by the senators they are attributed to.

item.title: GovBrief Today #556
item.description: Today Donald Trump maneuvered the lawyer who won his personal immunity case into the White House counsel's office, which represents the presidency. Will Scharf was one of Trump's personal lawyers who convinced the Supreme Court that presidents cannot be prosecuted for official acts. His reward comes two days after the Senate confirmed Todd Blanche, Trump's personal criminal defense lawyer from his hush money trial, as attorney general. Trump's personal defense team now runs the government's two most powerful legal offices. These jobs go to the people who pass the loyalty test, and the acceptable answer is written down now. Four judicial nominees testified on the Hill last week, and every one recited the same rehearsed script about the Electoral College rather than say who won the 2020 election. Senators narrowed the question to just the popular vote and got the script again. Blanche performed his version at his hearing, telling senators "I am the president's lawyer" before catching himself and saying "was."
